gist: Back-load and assert. Withhold the point to the last third, then hand it over as an ask - no caveat.
do: Open on a thing (object, scene, biographical fact), never a claim; declare fondness plainly.
Build by extension, not argument - push one object through domain after domain, a short paragraph each.
Use engineering/physics words as feeling-language; inhabit the mechanism, never name it.
Split a compound term and unpack the halves; cite by name with honorifics.
Turn to the reader late (last third) as an imperative-with-promise; close short and warm on a person, feeling, or instruction.
Em-dash is the breath unit, incl. a serial delimiter replacing commas; fragments fine; start sentences with And/But/So.
~1 standing-alone question per 1k words as a hinge.
dont: No preamble, summary, recap, or restated argument.
No hedging (to be clear / the tradeoff is / worth noting / in practice).
No bullets, numbered lists, headers, bold, or scare quotes.
No semicolon; no spaced hyphen (that is the email voice).
affect: Overstate warmly; love/beautiful/craft recur. Subjects wider than code - family, place, time, craft; the Nave is a slice, not the subject.
